criteria.title: Trace a material claim to its authority
criteria.startingState: A draft and evidence record contain a material claim with a source citation and pinpoint.
actions: Open the draft and locate the cited passage in the authority.
Check that the passage supports the claim and that jurisdiction, date, and relevant later treatment are accounted for.
criteria.expectedResult: Every material legal claim in the brief is traceable to a checked authority and pinpoint. The brief states the jurisdiction and cutoff date and distinguishes the authority's text from the researcher's interpretation.

criteria.title: Handle an unresolved authority
criteria.startingState: A synthetic draft relies on a citation that cannot be verified or an authority with unresolved later treatment.
actions: Review the claim and its evidence record.
Check how the draft handles the gap before release.
criteria.expectedResult: The draft names the gap and its effect on the conclusion. It omits or qualifies the affected claim and routes any remaining material uncertainty to the owner before release.

criteria.title: Verify the approved publication
criteria.startingState: The owner has approved a specific revision for a named audience, and the approved draft has been published.
actions: Open the saved brief using the intended reader's access.
Compare its claims and citations with the approved revision.
Inspect the visible page, linked files, and attachments for restricted material.
criteria.expectedResult: The reader can access the approved brief and its shareable references. Claims and citations match the approved revision, and restricted records, credentials, and review evidence are absent.

criteria.title: Hold publication when approval is missing
criteria.startingState: A draft is ready for release but the owner has not approved that revision.
actions: Compare the proposed revision against the owner's release record.
Check the destination for any release of the unapproved draft.
criteria.expectedResult: Release remains pending and the draft stays within the authorized working audience until the owner approves the specific revision.
